paragraphs: Rav Shemaya bar Ze'ira or Zeira.

Hyman describes him as a student of Abaye and Rava. In [Eruvin 93a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.93a.5), Rava sent a message to Abaye through Rav Shemaya bar Ze’ira; [Ketubot 81a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.81a.11) has bar Zeira.
And in [Chullin 116a](https://www.sefaria.org/Chullin.116a.4-5) Abaye resolved his difficulty for him.

He is also mentioned in [Pesachim 7a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.7a.10): Rav Shemaya bar Zeira explains that the markets of Jerusalem were swept every day. And in [Bava Metzia 26a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Metzia.26a.9) the reading is "bar Ze'ira."

[Kiddushin 76b](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.76b.8) has Rav Shimon bar Zeira reciting from the Kiddushin teachings of Levi’s school. Hyman gives the alternate reading Rav Shemaya. The supplied transcription has כה״ר at this point. The printed abbreviation appears to be סה״ד, and [Seder HaDorot 3508](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3508&lang=en) gives this emendation.[^4]

notes.text: כה״ר remains unidentified. The earlier draft’s “Rabbi Chayyim” was unsupported and has been removed. The alternative Shimon/Shemaya reading remains visible.

No new primary scalar was returned. Hyman describes him as a student of Abaye and Rava; this is not a new chronology finding. Rava sends to Abaye THROUGH Rav Shemaya; Abaye answers Shemaya’s question. Jerusalem’s markets are swept DAILY. Both Ze’ira/Zeira spellings and the distinct Shimon/Shemaya readings remain. כה״ר is unresolved, without an invented author, book or manuscript. All explicit full Rav titles are retained.

The printed Hyman article (vol. III, p. 1230) appears to abbreviate the source as סה״ד. In the consulted Seder HaDorot entry on Rav Shemaya bar Zeira, the author quotes the Shimon reading in Kiddushin 76b, calls it a copying error and proposes Shemaya. The consulted Kiddushin text itself reads Rav Shimon. The emendation is the author’s proposal, and this comparison does not establish a manuscript reading.

[Seder HaDorot 3508](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3508&lang=en) compares the spellings Zeira and Ze’ira, and proposes reading Shemaya in [Kiddushin 76b:8](https://www.sefaria.org/Kiddushin.76b.8). The consulted passage names Rav Shimon bar Zeira as the reciter from Levi’s school.
